name: slide-wright
description: Generate themed HTML slide decks, export to PowerPoint or PDF
readme:
slide-wright

Make presentations with your coding agent

Quick start · Examples · Export and share · Installation · FAQ

slide-wright is an agent skill that turns a topic, rough notes or an outline into a presentation. It designs a new theme for every deck and shows you two real slides in each direction before it builds the rest. The result is one HTML file. Present it in a browser, export it to PowerPoint or PDF, or deploy it to a live URL. slide-wright works in Claude Code, Codex, Cursor, OpenCode, Gemini CLI, Antigravity and other agents that support the `SKILL.md` format.

## Quick start In Claude Code, add the marketplace and install the plugin: ```bash /plugin marketplace add arifszn/slide-wright ``` ```bash /plugin install slide-wright ``` In any other agent: ```bash npx skills add arifszn/slide-wright ``` Then ask for a deck: ``` /slide-wright Make me a deck about ``` ## How it works ![Three steps: the prompt "/slide-wright Q3 board update for Corvid Labs, a B2B observability SaaS", the same two slides in three design directions with option 1 selected, and the full deck built in that direction](assets/how-it-works.png) 1. **Describe the deck.** A topic, rough notes or a full outline. The agent then asks how many design directions to compare and whether the slides should animate. 2. **Pick a direction.** Each direction gets its own palette, type and layout, shown on the same two slides of your deck: the title slide and one content slide. The previews open in your browser. If none fits, ask for new directions, or ask to adjust one ("warmer", "a bolder accent"). 3. **Get the full deck.** It builds the full deck in the direction you picked. Present it, change it later, export it or deploy it. ## What you get - **A theme made for the deck**: palette, typography, layout and a visual motif taken from the subject. There is no template library. - **Slides that make a point**: each content slide states one claim and backs it with a chart, flow, timeline, comparison, architecture diagram or metric panel, drawn in the theme's colors. - **Speaker notes and a presenter view**, and animation if you choose it. - **One self-contained HTML file**: no build step, and nothing to install to present it. Export it to PowerPoint or PDF, or deploy it to a live URL. ## Examples ![Three prompts, each in its own card above the title slide and one content slide it produced: "Create a Q3 board update for Corvid Labs, a B2B observability SaaS" with a scorecard title slide and a revenue chart; "Generate a presentation for ClickHouse, keep theme yellow" with black and yellow slides comparing row and column storage; "Create a presentation on MCP with this outline: [outline]" with a JSON-RPC title slide and an architecture diagram](assets/examples.png) ## Change a deck later Point the agent at a deck and ask for the change: a new slide, a rewrite, a different chart. It skips the preview step, since the look is already set, and runs the layout check again afterwards. This works on any deck built on reveal.js, including ones slide-wright did not make. ![The prompt "Add a pricing slide after slide 3" above a strip of five slides, where slide 4 is the new pricing slide in the same theme](assets/edit-later.png) ## Present it Open the HTML file in a browser. Move with the arrow keys, the space bar or a swipe. | Key | Action | | --- | --- | | F | Fullscreen | | Esc / O | Slide overview | | S | Speaker view with notes | | B / . | Pause to a black screen | | ? | Show all keys | ## Export and share ![Three prompts, each above what it produces: "Export my deck to PowerPoint" above a PowerPoint window with the slide title selected as an editable text box, "Export my deck to PDF" above a stack of PDF pages, and "Deploy my deck to a live URL" above a browser showing the deck at a surge.sh address](assets/export.png) ### PowerPoint Ask the agent, or run the exporter yourself. Text comes out as editable text boxes, with the speaker notes, and local videos are embedded. Shapes, charts and images are part of each slide's background picture: they look the same but are not editable. Fonts are not embedded, so on a machine without the deck's fonts PowerPoint substitutes similar ones. Use the PDF when exact typography matters. Animations are exported in their final state. To run the exporter yourself (Node 18 or newer; it uses Chrome or Edge, and downloads Chromium on first run if neither is installed): ```bash node /scripts/export-pptx.mjs deck.html ``` `` is the installed `slide-wright` folder. ### PDF The agent walks you through the browser's print dialog. To do it yourself, add `?print-pdf` to the deck's URL and open the print dialog (Cmd/Ctrl + P). Save as PDF with Landscape layout, margins set to None and background graphics on. ### Live URL The agent offers Surge, Vercel and Netlify and returns the URL. Each host needs a one-time login that you run in your own terminal; the agent gives you the command. To do it yourself, save the deck as `index.html` in an empty folder and upload the folder to any static host, such as GitHub Pages, Cloudflare Pages or S3. ## Installation [Quick start](#quick-start) covers the plugin and npx installs. You can also paste this to any agent that supports the `SKILL.md` format: ``` Fetch and follow the install instructions from https://raw.githubusercontent.com/arifszn/slide-wright/refs/heads/main/INSTALL.md ``` To copy the skill by hand, [INSTALL.md](INSTALL.md) lists the skills folder for each agent. ## FAQ **Does it use templates?** No. It designs each theme from the deck's subject and audience. When you reject the previews, it makes new directions that differ in palette, type and layout, not recolors of the same one. **Can I use my brand colors or fonts?** Yes. Put them in the prompt, as in "keep theme yellow" above, or ask it to adjust a preview. **Does the deck work offline?** It needs a connection to load the slide engine and fonts. For an offline copy, export a PDF or PPTX. ## Contributing Bug reports and pull requests are welcome. `npm test` runs the tests for the layout check and the PowerPoint exporter. After editing `slide-wright/SKILL.md`, run `tools/sync-root-skill.sh` to update the root copy; CI checks that they match. If slide-wright saved you time, [give it a star](https://github.com/arifszn/slide-wright). A star helps other people find it. ## License [MIT](LICENSE)

skillMd:
---
name: slide-wright
description: Create beautiful web presentations from a topic, rough notes, or an outline, and edit decks afterward — adding, removing, or revising slides. Asks how many design directions to preview and whether to animate, shows a two-slide preview of each custom theme, then builds the full deck only once the user picks a direction; edits to an existing deck skip that flow and apply in place. Use when the user wants to make slides, a presentation, a talk deck, a pitch deck, or to add/remove/change a slide in one that already exists.
---

# slide-wright

Turn a topic or rough notes into a boardroom-grade presentation: slides that read like a deck from a strong strategy or product team, delivered as a single self-contained HTML file that runs in any browser.


## The rule that defines this skill

Propose the look before you build the deck. On the first pass you never produce a finished presentation. You ask how many design directions the user wants to compare and whether they want animation, build a two-slide preview of each direction, and stop until the user picks one. Only then do you build the rest.

If the user says no, throw the directions out and try clearly different ones. Every theme is invented for the deck in front of you; there is no library of presets.

**New deck: read `slide-wright/references/new-deck.md` first.** It holds Steps 1-4 (work out the deck and ask the two questions, propose the look, get a yes, build) and the exact approval gate.

## The engine (keep this internal)

Decks render with reveal.js loaded from a CDN, but that is an implementation detail the user never sees. Talk about slides, themes, and design; the library name appears only inside the generated `<link>` and `<script>` tags. `slide-wright/references/deck-template.md` has the exact setup.

## Editing a deck that already exists

If the user points at an existing HTML deck, check whether it's built on reveal.js (look for the reveal.js `<link>`/`<script>` tags from a CDN). If it is — whether or not this skill built it — don't start over: read it, keep its theme, and make the change in place. The look is already approved, so skip the proposal and the gate. After editing, run `node <skill-dir>/scripts/check-deck.mjs <deck.html>` and fix every line it prints (`slide-wright/references/new-deck.md` has the details).

No reference files are needed for an edit, unless you add a new exhibit type (read `slide-wright/references/exhibits.md`) or code or animation (read `slide-wright/references/code-slides.md` or `slide-wright/references/motion-recipes.md`).

If the deck is HTML but not on reveal.js (different engine, plain slides, etc.), it's outside this skill's edit path — say so rather than forcing a rewrite onto a different engine. Everything else here is for building a new deck.

## Step 5 — Hand it off

1. Open the finished deck.
2. Say where it lives, the theme name, and the slide count.
3. Tell the user how to drive it: arrow keys, space, or swipe to move; **F** for fullscreen, **Esc** or **O** for the slide overview, **S** for the speaker view with notes; add `?print-pdf` to the URL and print to save a PDF (`slide-wright/references/export-pdf.md` has the steps); theme colors live in the `:root` variables, fonts in the `<link>`.
4. Offer the obvious next moves: revise the content, change the theme, export a PDF, export a PowerPoint file (`slide-wright/references/export-pptx.md`), or **deploy to a live URL** to share it. If they want to deploy, read `slide-wright/references/deploy.md` and let them pick the host (Surge, Vercel, or Netlify) — don't assume one.

## Reference files

Read each when you reach it, once; never all at once:

- `slide-wright/references/new-deck.md` — Steps 1-4 for a new deck
- `slide-wright/references/design.md` — inventing a theme and what makes a deck look designed (Step 2)
- `slide-wright/references/deck-template.md` — the HTML skeleton, layout, and engine setup (Step 2)
- `slide-wright/references/exhibits.md` — choosing and building the visual on each content slide (Step 2)
- `slide-wright/references/motion-recipes.md` — animation, when the user chose it (Step 2)
- `slide-wright/references/code-slides.md` — code slides and their markup contract (Step 4)
- `slide-wright/references/media.md` — images and video in slides (Step 4)
- `slide-wright/references/export-pdf.md` — saving a deck as a PDF (Step 5)
- `slide-wright/references/export-pptx.md` — exporting a deck to PowerPoint with editable text (Step 5)
- `slide-wright/references/deploy.md` — publishing the deck to a live URL (Step 5)
